chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Shaybah al-Zuhri, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A servant who is two-faced and has two tongues is bad. He will praise his believing brother in front of him, but talk badly about him in his absence. He will be jealous of him whenever he gets a blessing and will not assist him when a calamity befalls him.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of a two-faced person in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) identifies the 'two-faced' servant as a quintessential example of *riya* (showing off) and *hasad* (jealousy), highlighting the spiritual corruption of duplicity in social interactions. This description serves as a practical guide for Shia moral ethics, warning against the internal decay that accompanies external flattery and the failure to offer genuine support during adversity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-20 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khat’tab, on the authority of Ali ibn An-Nue’man, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Miskan, on the authority of Davood ibn Farqad, on the authority of Abi Shaybih az-Zahri that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) said, “

A servant who is two-faced and has two tongues is bad. He will praise his believing brother in front of him, but talk badly about him in his absence. He will be jealous of him whenever he gets a blessing and will not assist him when a calamity befalls him.”
